misconception: AI can't be delegated real work — you have to do everything yourself, step by step.

mentorLessons.line: Cowork is Claude's agentic workspace — the same engine that powers Claude Code, turned loose on knowledge work with no terminal required. You describe the outcome; it does the digging.
A remote session runs on Anthropic's servers in an isolated sandbox, not on your machine. Close the laptop, walk away — the work keeps going without you.
Claude only touches folders you've connected — never the whole drive. On desktop it reads and writes those files directly, no uploading and downloading by hand.
Don't hand-feed pebbles. State the outcome you want, and Cowork breaks the job into subtasks — even running parallel workstreams — and coordinates them itself.

Your tasks live in a list in the sidebar, and Claude reports the outcome — the finished spreadsheet, the memo — rather than narrating every swing of the pick. A push notification can fetch you when it's done or needs your go-ahead.
Cowork taps the same connectors, skills, and plugins as the rest of Claude. Connect your tools once and every dig can draw on them.
The ore that comes out is polished: Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint decks, formatted documents — real deliverables, not just chat text.

A scheduled task runs on its own cadence, remotely — your computer can be asleep and the shift still gets worked. Each run is its own session you can review, and you can pause, edit, or fire it on demand.
Be choosy about which tunnels you open. Keep credentials and financial records out of connected folders — a dedicated working folder is the safest shaft.
Projects group related tasks into workspaces with their own instructions, context, and memory — and what Claude learns in one project stays in that project.

questions.prompt: A teammate asks what Cowork actually is. What's the accurate answer?
choices: A chat mode with longer replies
A cloud drive for storing files
An agentic workspace where Claude executes complex, multi-step tasks on your behalf
A code editor for developers only
questions.reteach: Cowork is Claude's agentic workspace — you describe a desired outcome and Claude autonomously carries out the multi-step work.
hardChoices: A chat conversation with connectors enabled and a longer context window
A cloud file manager that organizes and syncs your connected folders
Claude Code's terminal, repackaged with a friendlier name for developers

questions.prompt: How does Cowork relate to Claude Code?
choices: It uses the same agentic architecture, brought to knowledge work without opening a terminal
There's no relation at all
Cowork is Claude Code with fewer capabilities
Cowork replaces Claude Code for programming
questions.reteach: Cowork runs on the same agentic architecture that powers Claude Code — aimed at knowledge work, no terminal needed.
hardChoices: It's a graphical wrapper that still needs the Claude Code CLI installed underneath
They share branding, but run on entirely separate architectures
It's Claude Code restricted to reading files rather than executing tasks

questions.prompt: You close your laptop in the middle of a remote Cowork session. What happens to the task?
choices: It dies instantly
It pauses until you reopen the laptop
Claude keeps working — remote sessions run on Anthropic's servers, not your machine
It silently restarts from the beginning
questions.reteach: Remote sessions run on Anthropic's servers in an isolated environment, so work continues even when your computer is closed.
hardChoices: It keeps running only while the Claude Desktop app stays open in the background
It checkpoints and resumes exactly where it stopped when you reopen the laptop
It continues, but any step that needs a connector is skipped until you return

questions.prompt: When a Cowork session on your desktop needs to execute code locally, where does that code run?
choices: Directly in your operating system with full access
In an isolated virtual machine on your device
On Anthropic staff computers
It refuses to ever run code locally
questions.reteach: Local code execution happens inside an isolated virtual machine on your device, walled off from the rest of your system.
hardChoices: In a sandboxed session on Anthropic's cloud servers, never on your device
Inside the Claude Desktop app's own process, using the app's permissions
In the browser's JavaScript sandbox, the same way artifacts run

questions.prompt: Claude needs to edit files on your computer during a Cowork task. What determines what it can access?
choices: It can browse your entire hard drive by default
Only files you attach one at a time in chat
Whatever was accessed in your last session
Only the folders you've explicitly connected
questions.reteach: File access is restricted to connected folders — Claude works directly in those without manual uploads, and touches nothing else.
hardChoices: Any folder on the drive, but it asks permission before each individual file
The folders you connected plus their parent directories for context
Whatever folders your project's custom instructions list as allowed

questions.prompt: A remote session needs a file from a folder you connected on your computer. What must be true for it to reach that file?
choices: Nothing — remote sessions can always reach your disk
The Claude Desktop app must be open on that computer
The file must be smaller than a set size limit
You must retype the file's contents into chat
questions.reteach: A remote session reaches your local folders through the Claude Desktop app — it only works while that app is open on your computer.
hardChoices: The folder must finish syncing to Anthropic's cloud before the session starts
Connected folders mirror to remote sessions automatically — nothing extra needed
You must approve the request from your phone each time the session asks

questions.prompt: You have a big research-and-report job. The Micromanager insists you feed Claude one tiny step at a time. What does Cowork actually support?
choices: Step-by-step spoon-feeding is the only way it works
Describing the desired outcome and letting Claude plan and execute the steps
Delegation, but only for coding tasks
Only tasks that finish within one reply
questions.reteach: Cowork is built for delegation — describe the outcome you want and Claude tackles the multi-step work autonomously.
hardChoices: Outcome delegation, but each subtask still needs your approval before it starts
It plans all the steps for you, but you carry out each one yourself
Full delegation, but only inside a project with custom instructions set up

questions.prompt: How does Cowork handle a complex job with several independent parts?
choices: Strictly one part at a time, always
It refuses jobs with more than one part
It makes you open a separate chat per part
It can divide the work into subtasks and run parallel workstreams
questions.reteach: Cowork coordinates sub-agents — complex work gets split into smaller tasks that can run in parallel for faster results.
hardChoices: It runs parts in parallel, but only if you open a separate session for each
It handles every part, but strictly in the order you listed them
Parallel workstreams exist, but only for coding jobs in Claude Code

questions.prompt: You delegated a task and walked away from your desk. How can you learn it finished?
choices: You can't — you must watch the screen the whole time
By reading raw server logs
A push notification on your phone when it's done or Claude needs your go-ahead
Tasks never complete while you're away
questions.reteach: Claude can notify your phone when a task finishes or needs approval — you don't have to babysit the screen.
hardChoices: A daily email digest summarizing every session's progress
The finished work waits unsent until you come back and confirm delivery
Keep the mobile app open in the foreground — progress only shows live

questions.prompt: Where do you find your running and completed Cowork tasks?
choices: The tasks list in the sidebar
A hidden configuration file
Only by asking support
They aren't viewable anywhere
questions.reteach: The sidebar's tasks list shows your tasks — and Claude messages you the outcome rather than narrating every step.
hardChoices: In a tasks.json file Claude maintains inside your connected folder
Only in the Claude Desktop app — web and mobile can't display tasks
In each project's custom instructions panel

questions.prompt: You want Cowork to pull data from your team's external tools while it works. How?
choices: Copy-paste the data into chat manually every time
Connectors — Cowork uses the same MCP connectors as the rest of Claude
Connectors don't function inside Cowork
Purchase a separate integration product
questions.reteach: Cowork supports the same connectors as other Claude products — connect a tool once and Cowork can draw on it mid-task.
hardChoices: Skills — they're the feature that links Claude to external tools
Reconnect each tool inside Cowork — chat connectors don't carry over
Export the data into a connected folder first; Cowork reads only local files

questions.prompt: Which of these can extend what Cowork is able to do?
choices: Connectors, skills, and plugins
Only connectors, nothing else
Nothing — Cowork's abilities are fixed
Only features you code yourself
questions.reteach: Cowork is extensible with connectors for your tools, skills for reusable workflows, and plugins that bundle both.
hardChoices: Connectors and skills, but plugins only work in Claude Code
Skills and plugins, but connectors stay a chat-only feature
Plugins alone — connectors and skills were folded into them

questions.prompt: Your boss wants a real deliverable, not a wall of chat text. What can Cowork hand back?
choices: Plain text only
Only images and screenshots
Only source code
Polished files — Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint decks, formatted documents
questions.reteach: Cowork produces professional outputs: spreadsheets with functional formulas, presentations, and formatted documents.
hardChoices: Formatted markdown you export to Office apps yourself
Spreadsheets and decks, but formulas arrive as static pasted values
Real files, but only written into connected folders, never delivered in chat

questions.prompt: You need a report compiled every Monday morning without asking for it each week. Best approach?
choices: Set a personal alarm and prompt Claude manually
Leave one chat window open forever
A scheduled task that runs automatically on a cadence
It can't be done in Cowork
questions.reteach: Scheduled tasks let Claude run recurring work automatically on the cadence you choose — no weekly re-prompting.
hardChoices: A project whose instructions tell Claude to run the report each Monday
A saved prompt template you re-send — Cowork can't start work unprompted
A recurring task, but you must open the app Monday to let it trigger

questions.prompt: Your computer is asleep when a scheduled task's time arrives. What happens?
choices: It runs anyway — scheduled tasks run remotely
It's skipped and never retried
It waits for your computer to wake up
The schedule gets deleted
questions.reteach: Scheduled tasks run remotely, so they fire on schedule even when your computer is asleep or the app is closed.
hardChoices: It runs only if the Claude Desktop app was left open before sleep
It runs remotely, but results are held until your computer comes back online
It's rescheduled to the same time the next day automatically

questions.prompt: After creating a scheduled task, how much control do you keep over it?
choices: None — it runs unchanged forever
You can pause, edit, run it on demand, review past runs, or delete it
You can only delete it by contacting support
You can rename it but nothing else
questions.reteach: Scheduled tasks stay under your control — edit the instructions or cadence, pause, run on demand, review runs, or delete.
hardChoices: You can pause or delete it, but instructions are locked once created
You can edit and pause it, but past runs aren't kept for review
Full control, except changing the cadence requires recreating the task

questions.prompt: You're picking a local folder to connect for a Cowork task. Which choice should give you pause?
choices: A dedicated working folder made for the task
An empty scratch folder
A folder of public press releases
A folder holding financial documents and credentials
questions.reteach: Be selective with folder access — keep financial documents, credentials, and personal records out; a dedicated working folder is safest.
hardChoices: A folder with thousands of files — too large for Claude to handle safely
A folder Claude already wrote outputs to in a previous session
A shared team folder of published meeting notes

questions.prompt: You run several recurring workstreams that need different rules and context. How do projects in Cowork help?
choices: They only change the visual theme
They merge all memory into one shared pool
Each project groups related tasks with its own instructions, context, and memory
They disable connectors for safety
questions.reteach: Projects are dedicated workspaces with their own instructions, context, and memory — what Claude learns in one project doesn't carry to others.
hardChoices: They group tasks visually, but instructions still apply account-wide
They store files and connectors per project, while memory stays global
They sync learned context across projects so nothing is repeated
